title: Exercise form guide
source: Training plan, section 10 (Strong templates, Oct 2026); 385 extra exercises (extra: true) written Nov 2026, reviewed

principles.title: Warm up the first lift, not every lift
principles.text: Ramp up on the first big press, row or squat of the day with 2–4 lighter sets of falling reps (your bench ramp of bar, 40, 60, 70 kg is a good model). Later exercises for the same muscles need one light feeler set at most.

principles.title: Stop 1–2 reps short of failure
principles.text: Most working sets should end when you could do 1–2 more clean reps. Isolation and machine moves (laterals, curls, leg extensions) can go to failure on the last set. Keep barbell bench and hack squat a rep shy so form holds.

principles.title: Control the lowering
principles.text: Take about 2–3 seconds on the way down and lift with intent. A controlled negative keeps tension on the muscle and makes reps comparable from week to week.

principles.title: Full range first, then load
principles.text: A rep only counts if it hits the same depth and lockout as last time. Add weight or reps only when the range stays the same. This is how your Strong numbers stay honest.

principles.title: Rest long enough on big lifts
principles.text: Rest about 2.5–3 minutes on bench, incline press, OHP, rows, pulldowns and hack squat, and 1–2 minutes on isolation work. Short rests cost reps, and reps are what you're trying to keep during a cut.

principles.title: Brace on anything heavy
principles.text: Breathe into your belly, tighten your midsection as if about to be poked, then do the rep. Breathe out near the top. This protects your lower back, which matters because your program avoids hinge lifts.

principles.title: During the cut
principles.text: Keep loads heavy and form identical. If a main lift drops two sessions in a row, check sleep, pre-workout food and volume before changing technique or calories.

principles.title: Log the setup, not just the weight
principles.text: Seat heights, foot placement and which machine you used change how heavy a weight feels. Add them to the exercise notes in Strong once so every session starts from the same position.

exercises.name: Bench Press (Barbell)
setup: Lie with your eyes under the bar. Feet flat and planted, a little behind your knees.
Grip just outside shoulder width so your forearms are vertical at the bottom. Squeeze the bar hard.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep a small arch in your upper back. Butt stays on the bench.
Unrack with straight arms and bring the bar over your shoulders.
steps: Take a breath and brace.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest, around nipple line. Elbows about 45–70° from your body, not flared straight out.
Touch the chest lightly. No bounce.
Press up and slightly back toward your face so the bar finishes over your shoulders. Drive your feet into the floor.
cues: Shoulder blades in your back pockets
Push yourself away from the bar
mistakes: Elbows flared to 90°, which loads the front of the shoulder.
Shoulder blades drifting apart as the set gets hard.
Bouncing off the chest or lifting the butt to finish a rep.
Touching higher on the chest each rep as you tire.
exercises.note: Bench without a spotter only inside a rack with safeties set just below chest height, or stop a full rep short of failure.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
setup: Set the bench to about 30°. Steeper than 45° turns it into a shoulder press.
Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, then kick them up one knee at a time as you lie back.
Shoulder blades back and down, chest up, feet planted.
steps: Start with the dumbbells over your upper chest, palms forward or turned slightly in.
Lower slowly until the handles are level with your chest and you feel a stretch. Elbows stay under your wrists, about 45° out.
Press up and slightly together, finishing over the upper chest. Don't clank the bells.
mistakes: Bench set too steep, so the shoulders do the work.
Cutting the range short as the weight goes up.
Dropping the dumbbells sideways at the end instead of bringing them back to the thighs.
exercises.note: To finish safely, bring the dumbbells to your chest, tuck your knees up, and rock back up to sitting with them on your thighs.

exercises.name: Gundam Chest Press (machine)
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with your mid to lower chest, not your neck.
Sit tall with your back on the pad, shoulder blades pulled back and down, feet flat.
If the machine has a start-position lever or foot bar, use it to get the handles into place without straining your shoulders.
steps: Brace and press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a good stretch across the chest. Keep your shoulder blades pinned.
Pause briefly in the stretch, then press again.
mistakes: Seat too low, so the handles sit near the neck and the shoulders take over.
Letting the stack bang between reps.
exercises.note: Use the same seat setting every time and note it in Strong so your numbers compare across weeks.

exercises.name: Cable Crossover
setup: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height, or a little higher.
Step forward into a split stance with a slight forward lean. Chest up.
Soft bend in the elbows. Keep that bend fixed for the whole set.
steps: Start with your arms out wide and a stretch across the chest.
Hug the handles together in an arc in front of your lower chest, as if wrapping a big tree.
Squeeze for a second, then let the arms open slowly back to the stretch.
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows, which turns it into a press.
Going so heavy that you have to lean and swing.
Short range: not opening up into the stretch.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
setup: Set the backrest upright or one notch back from vertical.
Kick the dumbbells up from your thighs to shoulder height.
Back flat against the pad, feet planted wide, ribs down.
steps: Start with the dumbbells at about ear to chin height, palms forward, elbows slightly in front of your body.
Brace and press up until your arms are straight and the bells are over your head.
Lower under control back to ear height.
cues: Head through the window at the top
mistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad to finish reps.
Stopping above ear height, so the range shrinks as you tire.
Elbows flared straight out to the sides.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (cable or dumbbell)
setup: Cable: set the pulley at hand or hip height. Stand side-on and hold the handle in the far hand so the cable runs across or behind your body.
Dumbbell: stand tall or lean slightly forward, bells by your sides.
Slight bend in the elbow. Shoulders down, away from your ears.
steps: Raise the arm out to the side, leading with the elbow, until it reaches about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly. Don't let the weight drop.
cues: Push the weight out, not up
Shoulders stay out of your ears
mistakes: Shrugging, which moves the work into the traps.
Swinging the body to start the rep.
Going too heavy. This muscle responds to clean reps, not big weights.
exercises.note: Your plan logs both Lateral Raise (Cable) on Push A and Side Delts on Push B at 7.5 kg. If Push B is dumbbells, the form is the same.

exercises.name: Standing Side Delt Machine
setup: Line your shoulder joint up with the machine's pivot point.
Place the pads on the outside of your upper arms or elbows. Chest against the pad if there is one.
Stand tall, shoulders down.
steps: Push the pads out and up with your elbows until your upper arms are about level with your shoulders.
Pause, then lower slowly to the start.
mistakes: Shoulder not lined up with the pivot, which makes the movement feel jerky.
Shrugging or leaning away from the machine to move more weight.
exercises.note: This replaced the front raise on Push A.

exercises.name: Front Raise (dumbbell)
setup: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing your legs or each other.
Soft knees, braced midsection, slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Raise the dumbbells straight in front of you to about shoulder height.
Pause, then lower slowly to the thighs.
cues: Stop at eye level at most
exercises.note: Your front delts already get plenty of work from bench, incline and overhead press. If you ever revisit Push B, this is the slot the plan suggests swapping for more laterals.

exercises.name: Reverse Fly (machine)
setup: Sit facing the pad. Set the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Set the handles so your arms start in front with a stretch in the back of the shoulders.
Neutral grip (palms facing in) or palms down, slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc until they are in line with your body.
Pause briefly, then return slowly.
mistakes: Squeezing the shoulder blades hard together, which turns it into an upper-back move.
Pulling the chest off the pad and using the back.
Bending the elbows more as the set goes on.

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Extension
setup: Overhead version: set the pulley low, face away from the stack, and bring the rope over your head. Staggered stance, slight lean forward.
Elbows point forward, about head width apart.
steps: Start with the elbows bent and your hands behind your head, feeling a stretch in the back of the arms.
Straighten the arms fully by moving only the forearms.
Return slowly to the stretch.
mistakes: Elbows flaring wide as the set gets hard.
Moving the upper arm, which turns it into a pullover.
exercises.note: Your log doesn't say whether this is done overhead. If you do it as a pushdown or across the body, use the pushdown cues and keep the elbows pinned.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (straight bar)
setup: Set the pulley high. Grip the bar overhand about shoulder width.
Stand close, slight forward lean, elbows tucked at your sides.
steps: Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze for a moment.
Let the bar rise until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor, elbows still at your sides.
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and the shoulders helping.
Leaning over the bar and pushing with body weight.
Letting the bar ride up to the face.

exercises.name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
setup: Set the pulley high and hold the rope with palms facing each other, thumbs up near the knobs.
Elbows at your sides, slight forward lean.
steps: Push the rope down and spread the ends apart at the bottom so your hands finish beside your thighs.
Squeeze, then let the rope rise slowly until your forearms pass parallel.
cues: Pull the rope apart at the bottom
mistakes: Elbows coming forward on the way up.
Short reps that never reach lockout.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (wide grip)
setup: Set the thigh pad so your legs are locked in snugly.
Grip the bar overhand, a little wider than shoulder width.
Sit down with arms fully straight and a stretch in your lats. Chest up, slight lean back (about 10–20°).
steps: Start by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Drive your elbows down toward your back pockets until the bar reaches your upper chest.
Pause, then let the bar rise slowly all the way to a full stretch.
cues: Chest up to meet the bar
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight with body swing.
Pulling the bar behind the neck.
Stopping short of the full stretch at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.equipment: Pulldown machine or cable, single handle
setup: Sit or kneel so the handle is directly overhead or slightly in front, with the arm fully stretched.
Neutral grip (palm facing in) usually feels best.
Brace with the free hand on your thigh or the machine.
steps: Let the arm reach up and slightly across so you feel a deep stretch down the side of your back.
Pull the elbow down and in toward your hip.
Pause, then return slowly to the full stretch.
mistakes: Rotating the body to move the weight.
Pulling with the biceps by curling the hand down.
Skipping the stretch at the top, which is where this variation pays off.
exercises.note: Do all reps on your weaker side first, then match the same reps on the other side.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.equipment: Low cable row, V-handle or bar
setup: Sit with feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit tall, chest up, back neutral.
Start with your arms straight and shoulders allowed to reach forward a little.
steps: Pull your shoulders back, then row the handle to your lower ribs or upper stomach.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a moment.
Return slowly, letting the arms straighten and the shoulders reach forward, without rounding your lower back.
mistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth by 30° or more to move the weight.
Rounding the lower back at the start of each rep.
Shrugging the handle toward the neck.
exercises.note: A small torso movement (about 10–15°) is fine. If you need more than that, the weight is too heavy for 8 clean reps.

exercises.name: Pullover Machine
setup: Set the seat so your shoulder joint lines up with the machine's pivot.
Put the pads on the back of your upper arms, hands lightly on the bar.
Belt or brace your hips so you stay seated.
steps: Start with arms up and back and a strong stretch in the lats.
Drive the elbows down in an arc until the bar reaches your stomach.
Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Push with the elbows, not the hands
mistakes: Pulling with the hands, which brings in the arms.
Arching the back at the top.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
setup: If your gym has a chest-supported T-bar, use it. Lie on the pad and grip the handles.
Free-standing version: straddle the bar, hinge forward to about 45°, knees soft, back flat and braced.
Close or neutral grip handle.
steps: Start with arms straight and a stretch through the upper back.
Row the handle toward your lower chest or upper stomach, elbows about 45° from your body.
Squeeze, then lower under control. Keep your torso angle the same throughout.
mistakes: Standing up more each rep to use momentum.
Short, choppy reps with a heavy load.
exercises.note: Your program leaves out hinge lifts, and the free-standing T-bar row loads the lower back. Use the chest-supported version if you can, or swap to a heavier Iso-Lateral Low Row on days your back feels tired.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Low Row (plate-loaded)
setup: Set the seat so the handles are in line with the bottom of your chest or a bit lower.
Chest against the pad, feet braced.
steps: Reach forward for a full stretch.
Pull the elbows back low and close to the body, toward your hips.
Pause, then return slowly. You can train one arm at a time.
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad to finish reps.
Shortening the reach at the front.

exercises.name: Shrug Machine
setup: Stand or sit under the pads or handles with arms straight and the load hanging.
Stand tall, chin neutral.
steps: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the top for a second.
Lower all the way down for a full stretch.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl
setup: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides, palms forward or turning forward as you lift.
Elbows by your sides, shoulders back.
steps: Curl the dumbbells up, turning the palms up, until the forearms are close to vertical.
Squeeze, then lower slowly all the way to straight arms.
cues: Pinky slightly higher than thumb at the top
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward so the shoulders lift the weight.

exercises.name: Seated Biceps Curl (machine)
setup: Set the seat so your armpits sit at the top edge of the pad.
Line your elbows up with the machine's pivot point.
steps: Curl the handles up until the biceps are fully shortened.
Lower slowly to almost straight arms.
mistakes: Lifting your elbows off the pad.
Dropping fast into the bottom, which stresses the elbow.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Curl
exercises.equipment: Low cable, straight bar, EZ bar or handles
setup: Set the pulley low. Stand facing the stack, a small step back so the cable pulls slightly forward.
Underhand grip, elbows by your sides.
steps: Curl up until your hands reach shoulder height.
Squeeze, then lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Fight it on the way down
mistakes: Letting the stack pull the arms down fast.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
setup: Back and hips flat against the pad, shoulders snug under the shoulder pads.
Feet shoulder width, middle of the platform. Toes slightly turned out.
Brace before you release the safety handles.
steps: Lower slowly, letting your knees travel forward over your toes.
Go as deep as you can while your hips stay on the pad. Aim for thighs at least parallel to the platform.
Drive up through your whole foot to just short of locking the knees.
mistakes: Knees caving inward on the way up.
Hips peeling off the pad at the bottom, which rounds the lower back.
Cutting depth as the weight goes up.
exercises.note: Lower foot placement puts more work on the quads. Use the same placement every session so numbers compare.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
setup: Bar across your upper back, not your neck. Grip just outside your shoulders.
Feet shoulder width, slightly in front of the bar so you sit straight down.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest squat depth.
steps: Brace and unrack by twisting the bar.
Sit down between your heels until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive up through the whole foot.
mistakes: Feet too far forward, which loads the lower back.
exercises.note: Smith machines vary in how heavy the bar is. Log the same machine every time.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
setup: Line your knee joint up with the machine's pivot.
Ankle pad sits just above the ankle, on the front of the shin.
Back against the pad, hold the side handles hard. Lean back slightly if the seat allows.
steps: Kick up until the legs are straight and squeeze the quads for a second.
Lower slowly until your knees are bent past 90°.
mistakes: Kicking the weight up and letting it drop.
Hips lifting off the seat as the weight gets heavy.
Short reps that skip the bottom stretch.
exercises.note: At 122 kg you are near the top of most stacks. When you max out the stack, add a pause at the top or slow down the lowering instead.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
setup: Lie face down with your knees just off the end of the pad, lined up with the pivot.
Pad just above the heels.
Hold the handles and press your hips into the bench.
steps: Curl your heels toward your butt as far as you can.
Squeeze, then lower slowly to almost straight legs.
mistakes: Hips lifting off the bench, which lets the lower back help.
exercises.note: This is your only direct hamstring exercise, so treat every rep seriously. Your plan mentions adding seated leg curls later if you want more hamstring work.

exercises.name: Hip Adductor Machine
setup: Sit tall with the pads on the inside of your knees.
Open the legs to a range that gives a stretch without pain.
steps: Squeeze the legs together until the pads meet.
Pause, then open slowly back to the stretch.
mistakes: Starting with a stretch that is too wide on the first set.
exercises.note: Adductors help a lot in squats. Increase the starting width gradually over a few sessions.

exercises.name: Hip Abductor Machine
setup: Sit with the pads on the outside of your knees.
Sit tall, or lean forward slightly to feel more of the glutes.
steps: Push the knees out as wide as you can.
Pause, then return slowly. Don't let the plates touch between reps.
mistakes: Rocking the torso to push out.
Short, fast reps with heavy weight.
exercises.note: 135 kg × 20 is likely the full stack. Make sets harder with a 2-second pause at the widest point instead of adding reps.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
setup: Pads on your shoulders, balls of your feet on the edge of the step.
Knees straight but not locked hard.
steps: Lower your heels as far as they go and hold the stretch for 1–2 seconds.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Calf Press on Seated Leg Press
loggedAs: Calf Press on Seated Leg Press
setup: Sit in the leg press and put the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform. Heels hang off.
Legs almost straight, knees soft.
steps: Let the platform push your toes back for a deep stretch. Hold 1–2 seconds.
Press through the balls of your feet as far as you can.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Feet slipping off the edge. Keep your shoes firmly on the platform.
Bending the knees to move the platform.
exercises.note: Keep the safety handles within reach and never remove your feet with the platform unlocked.

exercises.name: Seated Ab Crunch (machine)
setup: Set the seat so the handles or pads sit at chest or shoulder level.
Hook your feet under the rollers if there are any.
steps: Breathe out and curl your ribcage toward your hips, rounding your spine.
Squeeze for a second.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the abs.
mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of curling the spine.
Very light weight for very high reps.
exercises.note: Your plan still has this down as 5 kg × 100, to confirm. Abs grow like other muscles: pick a weight you can curl for 10–20 controlled reps.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk

baseline.value: 30 min at about 4.0 km/h, incline about 3

setup: Set the speed to about 4.0 km/h and the incline to about 3.
Have your Gatorade within reach.
steps: Walk tall with your normal stride and let your arms swing.
Keep the pace where you can still talk in full sentences.
mistakes: Holding the handrails, which cuts the work by a lot.
exercises.note: This is for burning calories while recovering. If your legs are trashed after Lower A or B, keep the time and lower the incline.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
setup: Sit on the floor with both knees bent about 90°, feet a little wider than hip width.
Put your hands on the floor behind you, or hold them in front of you if you can sit tall without them.
steps: Let both knees drop to one side so the front leg and back leg each make a 90° angle.
Pause, then lift the knees and rotate them through the middle to the other side.
Keep the movement slow and smooth, side to side.
cues: Turn from the hips, not the lower back
mistakes: Rounding the lower back and collapsing backward.
Forcing the back knee down when the hip is stiff.
Rushing and swinging the legs over.
exercises.note: Stop if you feel a pinch at the front of the hip. Work in the range you can control and let it grow over time.

exercises.name: Adductor / Groin Stretch
setup: Sit tall and press the soles of your feet together, knees out to the sides.
Hold your ankles, heels as close to you as is comfortable.
steps: Let your knees fall toward the floor.
Lean forward from the hips with a flat back.
Hold for 20–30 seconds and breathe.
mistakes: Rounding the back to get lower.
Pressing hard on the knees with the hands.
exercises.note: Hold a steady stretch, never a sharp pull. Back off if the inside of your knee hurts.

exercises.name: Alternate Hammer Curl (Dumbbell)
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Elbows at your sides.
steps: Curl one dumbbell up with the palm still facing in, thumb toward your shoulder.
Lower it all the way under control.
Repeat with the other arm.
mistakes: Swinging the body to start the rep.
Elbow drifting forward at the top.
exercises.note: Keep the elbows pinned and lower under control; a swinging hammer curl with heavy dumbbells loads the elbow tendons.

exercises.name: Arc Trainer (Machine)
setup: Step onto the pedals and hold the fixed handles lightly.
Set a resistance and incline you can keep for the whole session.
steps: Push the pedals forward and down through a smooth arc with even strides.
Keep your weight over the middle of each foot.
Stay upright and keep a steady pace you could hold a conversation at.
mistakes: Leaning your bodyweight on the handles so the legs do less.
Locking the knees at the end of each stride.
Starting at a resistance that makes your form fall apart after a few minutes.
exercises.note: Start with a few easy minutes, and slow down if your knees or hips feel pinched.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
setup: Start in a push-up with your hands much wider than shoulder width, fingers turned slightly out.
Body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Lower toward one hand, bending that elbow while the other arm stays nearly straight.
Push back to the middle.
Alternate sides or do all reps on one side.
mistakes: Hips sagging or twisting toward the working side.
Flaring the working elbow straight out.
exercises.note: Build up from regular and wide push-ups first. Raise the hands on a bench to make it easier.

exercises.name: Arm Circles (Front & Back)
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Raise your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down.
steps: Make small forward circles with straight arms.
Slowly make the circles bigger over 10 to 15 seconds.
Reverse and circle backward the same way.
cues: Shoulders down, away from your ears
mistakes: Shrugging your shoulders up as the circles get bigger.
Rushing so the circles get small and sloppy.
Arching your lower back to get the arms back.
exercises.note: This is a warm-up. Keep it easy, and stop if you feel pain at the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Arnold Press (Dumbbell)
setup: Sit with your back supported and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with your palms facing you.
Keep your feet flat and your core braced.
steps: Press the dumbbells up while rotating your palms to face forward.
Lock out overhead.
Lower while rotating your palms back toward you.
mistakes: Arching your lower back as you press.
Rushing the rotation so the weights swing.
Letting your elbows flare too far back.
exercises.note: Use lighter weights than a standard shoulder press, and set the dumbbells down on your thighs when you finish.

exercises.name: Assault Bike (Machine)
setup: Set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Hold the moving handles and sit tall.
steps: Push and pull the handles while you pedal, so arms and legs work together.
Hold a steady effort, or work hard for a set time and then ease off.
Finish with a few minutes of easy pedalling.
cues: Push with the legs, pull with the arms
mistakes: Seat set too low, which cramps the knees at the top of each stroke.
Starting every interval flat out and fading in the second round.
exercises.note: The fan resistance rises with effort, so sprints get hard very quickly. Start with short intervals and stop if you feel faint.

exercises.name: B-Stance Hip Thrust
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a bench.
Plant one foot flat with the shin vertical at the top, and rest the other foot lightly on its toes or heel.
steps: Drive through the heel of the main foot to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Pause and squeeze your glute at the top.
Lower under control and finish all reps on one side.
cues: Heel of the main foot drives
mistakes: Arching your lower back to get higher instead of squeezing the glute.
Pushing hard through the back foot so the main leg does less.
Letting your hips twist toward the lifted side.
exercises.note: Do all reps on your weaker side first, then match the number on the other side.

exercises.name: Curls (Backpack)
setup: Pack the bag tight so the weight cannot shift, and check the handle or straps are strong.
Hold it by the top handle with both hands in front of your thighs, elbows at your sides.
steps: Curl the bag toward your chest without moving your elbows.
Squeeze at the top for a moment.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
cues: Elbows stay pinned to your ribs
mistakes: Swinging the bag up with your hips and back.
Dropping the bag quickly at the bottom.
exercises.note: Check the handle and zip before you start, as a failing strap can drop the load onto your feet.

exercises.name: Row (Backpack)
setup: Pack the bag tight and grip its handle or straps.
Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back and soft knees, with the bag hanging below your chest.
steps: Pull the bag toward your lower ribs, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight again.
mistakes: Standing up taller as you pull.
Rounding the upper back as the set gets hard.
Jerking the bag off the bottom.
exercises.note: Check the bag's straps before use, and keep your back flat rather than adding more weight.

exercises.name: Backstroke Swim
setup: Float on your back with your ears in the water and your hips near the surface.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and your belly tight.
steps: Reach one arm overhead and enter the water pinky first.
Pull that arm down by your side under the water while the other arm reaches over.
Flutter kick from the hips with long, loose legs and keep rotating slightly side to side.
cues: Rotate a little with each stroke
mistakes: Sitting in the water with the hips sinking.
Bending the knees too much on the kick.
exercises.note: Swim only where you can do so safely, ideally with a lifeguard on duty or someone nearby.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up (Band)
setup: Loop the band over the bar and secure it by pulling one end through the other.
Put one knee or foot in the bottom of the band and grip the bar just wider than your shoulders.
steps: Start from a full hang with your arms straight and shoulders down.
Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
mistakes: Kicking or bouncing off the band so the arms do less.
Half reps that start from bent arms.
Shrugging your shoulders to your ears at the top.
exercises.note: Check the band is seated securely on the bar, and step out of it carefully. Use a lighter band as you get stronger.

exercises.name: Curl (Band)
setup: Stand on the middle of the band with your feet hip width apart.
Hold the ends or handles with palms forward, elbows at your sides.
steps: Curl your hands to your shoulders without moving your elbows.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
cues: Fight the band on the way down
mistakes: Letting the band snap your arms down.
Leaning back to get the last few inches.
Elbows swinging forward as the band gets tight.
exercises.note: Check the band for nicks or cracks before use, and keep it away from your face in case it snaps.

exercises.name: External Rotation (Band)
setup: Anchor the band at elbow height and stand side-on with the band in your far hand.
Bend your elbow to 90° and pin it to your side, with a rolled towel between elbow and ribs if you like.
steps: Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping the elbow in place.
Pause briefly at the end of the range.
Return slowly to the start.
cues: Turn the forearm, don't pull the shoulder
mistakes: Elbow drifting away from your body.
Twisting your whole torso to move the band.
Using a band so tough you can't control it.
exercises.note: Use light tension. Stop if you feel a pinch or pain deep in the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge (Band)
setup: Lie on your back with a mini band just above your knees.
Plant your feet flat, hip width apart, close to your hips.
steps: Press your knees slightly out against the band.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze for a moment at the top, then lower under control.
cues: Knees press out into the band
mistakes: Knees collapsing inward as you lift.
Arching your lower back to get your hips higher.
Pushing through your toes instead of your heels.
exercises.note: Check the mini band for nicks before use, and stop if it rolls or digs into your knees.

exercises.name: Good Morning (Band)
setup: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip width apart.
Loop the other end behind your neck and over your upper back, holding it at your shoulders.
steps: Soften your knees and push your hips back with a flat back.
Lower your torso until it is about parallel to the floor or you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Squeeze your glutes to drive your hips forward and stand tall.
mistakes: Rounding your back to reach lower.
Bending the knees so it turns into a squat.
Letting the band sit on your neck instead of your upper back.
exercises.note: Check the band is anchored securely under your feet and has no nicks, and keep the range small if your lower back is sore.

exercises.name: High Face Pull (Band)
setup: Anchor the band above head height. Hold an end in each hand with palms facing down and step back until it is tight.
Stand tall with your ribs down and a slight knee bend.
steps: Pull the band toward your forehead with your hands travelling out to the sides.
Finish with elbows high and fists near your ears.
Return slowly to straight arms.
cues: Pull the band apart as you pull it back
Squeeze the back of your shoulders
mistakes: Leaning back to move the band.
Shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.
Letting your elbows drop so it becomes a row.
exercises.note: Use a light band. This is a shoulder-health move, so stop if your shoulders pinch.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction (Band)
setup: Put a mini band around your thighs or just above your knees.
Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, holding a support if you need it.
steps: Move one leg out to the side against the band, toes pointing forward.
Pause at the top.
Return slowly without letting the band snap the leg back.
mistakes: Leaning your upper body sideways to get the leg higher.
Turning your toes up and swinging the leg.
Letting the band pull your knee in on the way back.

exercises.name: Kneeling Pulldown (Band)
setup: Anchor the band high. Kneel facing it, holding an end in each hand, arms straight overhead.
Sit tall, ribs down.
steps: Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down for a moment.
Let your arms rise slowly back up.
cues: Elbows down to your back pockets
mistakes: Leaning far back to finish the rep.
Pulling with your hands instead of your elbows.
exercises.note: Make sure the anchor is secure and cannot slip, since a failing anchor snaps the band toward you.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Band)
setup: Stand on the middle of the band, with an end or handle in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
steps: Raise both arms out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Swinging your hips to get the band up.
Letting the band yank your arms down.
exercises.note: Check the band for nicks before use and keep it away from your face.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Band)
setup: Anchor the band low and loop the other end around one ankle.
Lie face down, or stand facing the anchor holding a support.
steps: Bend your knee to pull your heel toward your glute.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly without letting the band snap your leg straight.
mistakes: Lifting your hips or arching your lower back.
Letting the band whip the leg back.
exercises.note: Check the band is anchored securely and that nothing can slip when it stretches.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Band)
setup: Stand on the band with feet hip width apart and hold the ends at your shoulders, palms forward.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
steps: Press up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower to your shoulders slowly.
Keep tension on the band at the bottom.
mistakes: Leaning back to finish the press.
The band slipping out from under a foot.
Flaring elbows too far behind the body.
exercises.note: Keep the band clear of your face and replace it if you see nicks.

exercises.name: Pull-Through (Band)
setup: Anchor the band low behind you. Face away from the anchor and hold the band between your legs, then step out until it is tight.
Stand with feet hip width apart.
steps: Hinge at the hips and let the band pull your hands back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
mistakes: Leaning back at the top instead of finishing with the hips.
Letting the band pull your back into a round.
exercises.note: Anchor the band securely and check it for nicks before use, since a snapping band can hit you.

exercises.name: Pullover (Band)
setup: Anchor the band behind your head. Lie on your back with straight arms above your face and the band in both hands.
Feet flat, ribs down.
steps: Pull the band in an arc over your chest toward your hips.
Keep your elbows nearly straight.
Return slowly overhead.
mistakes: Bending your elbows into a pushdown.
Arching your back as the band pulls you.
Letting the band yank your arms overhead.
exercises.note: Anchor the band securely and keep it clear of your face as you pull.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Band)
setup: Stand on the band with feet hip width apart and hold the ends in front of your thighs.
Slight bend in the knees.
steps: Push your hips back with a flat back, keeping the band close to your legs.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
mistakes: Letting the band drift away from your legs.
exercises.note: Stop the lowering when your back starts to round, not when the band tightens.

exercises.name: Row (Band)
setup: Anchor the band at chest height. Sit or stand facing it with an end in each hand.
Sit tall with your arms straight and shoulders down.
steps: Pull your hands toward your lower ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms go forward slowly.
mistakes: Letting the band yank your shoulders forward.

exercises.name: Seated Pulldown (Band)
setup: Anchor the band above you. Sit on the floor or a bench facing it with your arms straight up.
Chest up.
steps: Pull your elbows down toward your ribs.
Squeeze for a second.
Let your arms rise slowly.
mistakes: Leaning back to finish the pull.
Pulling with the hands instead of the elbows.
exercises.note: Make sure the anchor point is secure before you pull.

exercises.name: Shoulder Dislocates (Band)
setup: Hold a band or dowel with a wide grip in front of your hips.
Stand tall with ribs down.
steps: Lift your arms overhead and behind your body with straight elbows.
Bring them back to the front by the same path.
Narrow your grip slightly if it feels tight.
mistakes: Gripping too narrow, which forces the shoulders into pain.
Arching your lower back to get the arms over.
exercises.note: Move slowly and widen your grip if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Shrug (Band)
setup: Stand on the band with feet hip width apart and the ends in your hands at your sides.
Keep your arms straight and ribs down.
steps: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Letting the band snap your shoulders down.
exercises.note: Check the band for nicks and stand firmly on it before shrugging.

exercises.name: Single Arm Lateral Raise (Band)
setup: Stand on one end of the band and hold the other end with the opposite hand.
Stand tall with a slight elbow bend.
steps: Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Pause for a moment.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Leaning away from the lifting arm.
Letting the band pull your arm down quickly.
exercises.note: Check the band for nicks and keep your foot planted on it.

exercises.name: Squat (Band)
setup: Stand on the middle of the band with feet shoulder width apart.
Hold the ends at your shoulders with elbows forward.
steps: Sit down between your heels until your thighs are about parallel.
Pause.
Push through your whole foot to stand up.
mistakes: The band slipping out from under your feet.
exercises.note: Stand on the band with both feet and check it for nicks before use, because a snapping band can hit you; keep the band's ends away from your face.

exercises.name: Tricep Kickbacks (Band)
setup: Hold the band and hinge forward slightly.
Pin your upper arm against your side with the elbow bent.
steps: Straighten your elbow and push your hand back.
Squeeze at lockout.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Rushing so the band does the work.
exercises.note: Check the band for nicks before use and keep your free hand clear of its path.

exercises.name: Wood Chopper (Band)
setup: Anchor the band high and stand side-on to it.
Hold the band with both hands and keep your feet shoulder width apart.
steps: Pull the band diagonally across your body from high to low.
Rotate from your torso and hips.
Return slowly with control.
mistakes: Letting the band spin you back around.
exercises.note: Anchor the band securely at the high point and check it for nicks before pulling.

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Mobilization (Band)
setup: Loop the band around your ankle just below the bone, anchored behind you.
Kneel or stand in a split stance with the working foot forward.
steps: Push your front knee forward over your toes while the heel stays down.
Pause at the end of the range.
Return slowly.

exercises.name: Clamshell (Band)
setup: Lie on your side with your knees bent and a mini band above your knees.
Stack your hips and keep your feet together.
steps: Keep your feet together and lift the top knee.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Letting the band snap the knee back.
exercises.note: Check the mini band for nicks before use.

exercises.name: Eccentric Tibialis Raise (Band)
setup: Sit with your leg out and loop the band over the top of your foot, anchored in front of you.
Keep your heel on the floor.
steps: Pull your toes up toward your shin.
Hold for a moment.
Lower slowly against the band for three to four seconds.
mistakes: Letting the band yank your foot down.
exercises.note: Anchor the band securely and check it for nicks before use.

exercises.name: Banded Back Squat (Barbell)
setup: Loop the bands over the bar ends and anchor them to the base of the rack, checking both sides are the same tension.
Set the bar on your upper back, feet shoulder width apart, toes slightly out.
steps: Brace your core and sit down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Pause for a beat at the bottom.
Drive up hard through your whole foot, staying strong as the band tension rises near the top.
cues: Chest up as the bands pull you down
mistakes: Letting the bands pull you forward onto your toes.
Knees caving inward as the tension builds.
Shortening the depth because the bottom feels easy.
exercises.note: Set the rack safeties just below your bottom position, and check the bands are anchored securely and not frayed before loading.

exercises.name: Behind The Back 30 Degree Shrug (Barbell)
setup: Hold the bar behind your thighs with an overhand grip, hands just outside your hips.
Stand tall with your chest up and a slight lean back.
steps: Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears, keeping your arms straight.
Hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are long again.
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles instead of lifting straight up.
Bending your elbows to help the lift.
Leaning forward so the bar drags your back into a round.
exercises.note: Use a grip you trust and set the bar down on pins or on the floor by bending your knees, not rounding your back.

exercises.name: Bent Over Row - Overhand (Barbell)
setup: Stand with feet hip width apart over the bar and grip it overhand just outside your knees.
Hinge until your torso is about 45° and brace, with the bar hanging below your chest.
steps: Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control until your arms are straight again.
cues: Flat back from head to tailbone
mistakes: Standing up taller as the set gets hard, which turns the row into a shrug.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Jerking the bar off your legs with momentum.
exercises.note: Brace your core on every rep and drop the weight once your back starts rounding, since the lower back carries the load here.

exercises.name: Clean And Jerk (Barbell)
setup: Stand with feet hip width apart and the bar over your midfoot, shins touching it.
Grip just outside your knees with a hook grip, shoulders slightly over the bar.
steps: Pull the bar off the floor, keeping it close to your legs.
Extend powerfully, then drop under the bar to catch it on your front shoulders in a squat.
Stand up, dip, drive the bar overhead and land in a split stance, then lower the bar back down.
cues: Dip straight down before the jerk
mistakes: Letting the bar swing out in front of you.
Pressing the bar out instead of dropping under it.
Catching the clean with your elbows low so the bar rolls forward.
exercises.note: This is a technical Olympic lift. Learn it with a coach or an empty bar first, and always use bumper plates on a platform so you can drop a missed lift safely.

exercises.name: Clean And Press (Barbell)
setup: Stand with feet hip width apart and the bar over your midfoot.
Grip just outside your knees and set your back flat.
steps: Pull the bar off the floor and clean it to your front shoulders.
Stand tall, brace your core, and press the bar overhead to lockout.
Lower the bar to your shoulders, then back down to the floor.
mistakes: Leaning back on the press to finish the rep.
Pulling the bar away from your body in the clean.
Pressing before you are fully stable on your feet.
exercises.note: Start with an empty bar and learn the clean before adding weight. Use bumper plates so a missed lift can be dropped safely.

exercises.name: Front Rack Step Up Knee Drive (Barbell)
setup: Rest the bar on your front shoulders in a rack position with your elbows high.
Face a knee-height box with feet hip width apart.
steps: Step up with one foot and drive through that heel until you stand tall.
Lift the back knee up to hip height.
Lower the back foot under control and repeat on the same side.
mistakes: Pushing off the back foot instead of the front leg.
Letting your elbows drop so the bar rolls forward.
Leaning forward to throw the knee up.
exercises.note: Use a box low enough that your hips stay level and keep the rack position solid before adding load; set the bar down from a rack, not from the floor.

exercises.name: High Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
setup: Set the bench to a steep incline, around 45° to 60°.
Lie back with your shoulder blades pulled together and your feet planted, and grip a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Unrack the bar and lower it to the top of your chest, elbows about 45° to 70° from your body.
Press up and slightly back until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned the whole time.
cues: Drive your feet into the floor
mistakes: Letting the bar drift toward your neck.
Lifting your butt off the bench to finish a rep.
exercises.note: Use a spotter or rack safeties set just below chest height, since a steep angle makes the shoulders carry more of the load.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch (Barbell)
setup: Use a wide snatch grip and stand with feet hip width apart.
Hold the bar at mid-thigh with arms long.
steps: Extend your hips and shrug.
Pull your elbows high and turn the bar overhead without dropping into a squat.
Lock out overhead, then lower the bar to your thighs with control.
mistakes: Casting the bar away from your body.
Lowering the bar in a crash.
exercises.note: This is a technical lift. Start with a light bar or a dowel, and use a platform and bumper plates if you ever drop the bar.

exercises.name: Power Snatch (Barbell)
setup: Use a wide grip with your hips lower than your shoulders and the bar over your midfoot.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
steps: Pull from the floor and extend hard through your hips.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it overhead in a quarter squat.
Stand up with the bar locked out overhead.
mistakes: Letting the bar swing out in front of you.
Catching the bar with bent arms.
Pulling with your arms before your hips extend.
exercises.note: Learn this with a coach and bumper plates on a platform where a missed lift can be dropped safely.

exercises.name: Pullover (Barbell)
setup: Lie across or along a bench holding a light bar above your chest with straight arms.
Keep your feet flat and your ribs down.
steps: Lower the bar back over your head with soft elbows, stretching your lats.
Pause when you feel a stretch.
Pull the bar back over your chest in the same arc.
mistakes: Bending your elbows so it becomes a press.
Arching your lower back hard at the bottom.
exercises.note: Use a light weight with a spotter, and stop if you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Skullcrusher (Barbell)
exercises.equipment: Barbell or EZ bar, flat bench
setup: Lie on a flat bench holding the bar above your chest with straight arms.
Keep your feet planted and your upper arms vertical.
steps: Bend only your elbows and lower the bar toward your forehead.
Pause just above your forehead.
Straighten your elbows to return.
mistakes: Letting the bar drift back over your head and turning it into a pullover.
Bouncing the bar off the forehead.
exercises.note: Use a spotter or a lighter weight than your press, since a slipped grip or missed rep can land the bar on your face.

exercises.name: Snatch (Barbell)
setup: Take a wide snatch grip with the bar over midfoot.
Chest up, back flat, shoulders slightly over the bar.
steps: Lift the bar off the floor, keeping it close to your body.
Extend and pull yourself under the bar into a full overhead squat.
Stand up with the bar locked out overhead.
mistakes: The bar looping out in front of you.
Letting your elbows bend in the catch.
Rushing the pull before your hips extend.
exercises.note: This is a highly technical lift. Practise the overhead squat with a dowel first and always use bumper plates on a platform.

exercises.name: Spinal Jefferson Curl (Barbell)
setup: Stand on a low step with a very light bar held in front.
Feet hip width apart, soft knees.
steps: Tuck your chin and slowly curl your spine downward one segment at a time.
Lower only as far as your hamstrings and back allow.
Reverse slowly to stand tall.
cues: Round one segment at a time
exercises.note: Only use a very light load and stop immediately if you feel any pain in your back, as this deliberately rounds the spine.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge (Barbell)
setup: Set the bar on your upper back and unrack it, then step back with feet hip width apart.
Keep your chest up and core braced.
steps: Step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push off the front foot to bring the back foot through.
Alternate legs while walking.
mistakes: Taking short steps that push the knee far past the toes.
exercises.note: Walk in a clear area, rack the bar with both feet planted, and start with an empty bar until your balance is steady.

exercises.name: Battle Ropes
setup: Anchor the rope at its middle and hold one end in each hand, standing a few steps back so the ropes sit slightly slack.
Take a quarter-squat stance with your chest up and core braced.
steps: Raise and drop one arm, then the other, making fast alternating waves.
Keep the waves travelling all the way to the anchor.
Work for 15 to 30 seconds, then rest.
mistakes: Rounding your back and collapsing over the ropes.
Moving only your arms and forgetting the legs.
Letting the waves die out halfway.
exercises.note: Check the anchor is secure and the floor is clear, and stop a set if your grip or lower back gives out.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley low and stand facing away from the stack, one handle in your hand.
Step forward so the cable runs behind you and your arm starts slightly behind your torso.
steps: Curl the handle forward and up toward your shoulder, keeping your elbow behind your body.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is nearly straight again.
mistakes: Letting your elbow swing forward and turning it into a normal curl.
Leaning forward to get the weight up.
Dropping the weight stack at the bottom.
exercises.note: Start light, because the stretched position at the bottom loads the biceps tendon hard.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
setup: Start on your hands and toes with your knees bent and hovering just off the floor.
Keep your back flat and your hips low, level with your shoulders.
steps: Move your right hand and left foot forward together.
Then move your left hand and right foot.
Keep crawling for a set distance or time.
mistakes: Letting your hips rise into the air.
Rushing so your knees bump the floor.
Dragging your feet instead of stepping.
exercises.note: Clear the space and use a non-slip floor; stop if your wrists hurt.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Neck Press (Barbell)
setup: Sit upright on a bench with back support, or stand, with the bar resting on your upper traps behind your neck.
Take a grip wider than your shoulders and brace your core.
steps: Press the bar straight up until your arms are locked out.
Lower it under control to ear level, then stop.
Press again without bouncing.
mistakes: Lowering the bar past ear level.
Pushing your head forward as the bar rises.
Using more weight than your shoulders can control.
exercises.note: Only do this if your shoulders have full overhead mobility, use light weight and safeties, and stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder or neck.

exercises.name: Belt Squat (Machine)
setup: Fasten the belt snugly around your hips and stand on the platforms with feet shoulder width apart.
Keep your chest tall and hold the handles for balance.
steps: Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Drive up through your whole foot until you stand tall.
mistakes: Lifting your heels at the bottom.
exercises.note: Check that the belt is tight before you unlock the weight, and keep it low on your hips rather than your waist.

exercises.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row (Barbell)
setup: Straddle the long bar and hinge forward with a flat back.
Hold the bar close to the weighted end with one hand and rest your other hand on your thigh.
steps: Row the bar up toward your hip, driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is nearly straight.
mistakes: Twisting your torso to heave the weight.
Rounding your back as you tire.
Dropping the bar at the bottom.
exercises.note: Make sure the bar end is held securely in the corner or landmine so it can't slip.

exercises.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row Palms In (Dumbbell)
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Hinge forward from the hips until your torso is about 45° and your back is flat.
steps: Row both dumbbells toward your ribs, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Standing up taller as you pull.
Letting your shoulders round forward at the bottom.
exercises.note: Keep a strong brace, and lower the dumbbells to the floor by bending your knees if your back tires.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise
setup: Stand with your toes on the edge of a step or on flat ground, knees bent about 30°.
Hold a wall or rail for balance.
steps: Raise your heels as high as you can while keeping your knees bent.
Hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
mistakes: Straightening the knees and turning it into a standing calf raise.
Rolling to the outside of the foot.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Alternating Lateral Lunge
setup: Stand tall with your feet together and your hands in front of your chest.
Keep your toes pointing forward.
steps: Step wide to one side and sit your hips back, bending that knee.
Keep the other leg straight and its foot flat.
Push through the working foot to return to the middle, then alternate sides.
mistakes: Letting the working knee cave in.
Lifting the heel of the working foot.
Rounding your back as you sit.
exercises.note: Keep the step small if your inner thighs feel tight, and hold a support if your balance is shaky.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Alternating Reverse Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Hands on your hips or in front of your chest.
steps: Step one foot backward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front shin about vertical.
Push through your front heel to return to standing, then alternate.
mistakes: Letting your front knee travel far forward.
Rushing so the back knee bangs the floor.
exercises.note: Use a mat under the back knee and hold a support if your balance needs it.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Box Squat
setup: Stand in front of a box or bench with feet shoulder width apart.
Reach your arms forward for balance.
steps: Sit your hips back until you lightly touch the box.
Pause without relaxing on it.
Drive through your heels to stand tall.
mistakes: Dropping onto the box and bouncing back up.
Rounding your back at the bottom.
exercises.note: Use a stable box that won't slide, and keep your weight in your feet rather than resting on the box.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Deadlift
setup: Stand with your feet hip width apart and your hands in front of your thighs.
Keep your chest up and your knees soft.
steps: Push your hips back and hinge forward with a flat back.
Slide your hands down your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
mistakes: Rounding your back to reach lower.
exercises.note: Stop the lowering when your hamstrings tighten or your back starts to round.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Deficit Reverse Lunge
setup: Stand on a low step with feet hip width apart.
Keep your hands on your hips.
steps: Step one foot backward off the step and lower your back knee.
Keep your front shin steady as you go down.
Drive through your front heel to return to the step.
mistakes: Letting the front knee cave in.
exercises.note: Use a stable low step and hold a support until your balance is steady.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Elevated Push Up
setup: Place your hands on a stable raised surface slightly wider than shoulders, feet on the floor behind you.
Make a straight line from your head to your heels.
steps: Lower your chest toward the surface with your elbows about 45° from your body.
Pause.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.note: Make sure the bench can't slide, and use a higher surface if you can't keep a straight body.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Hip Abduction
setup: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked.
Rest your head on your arm and keep your top hand in front for balance.
steps: Lift your top leg a few inches without rolling your hips back.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the leg too high with your lower back.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Knee Push Ups
setup: Kneel with your hands under your shoulders and knees on a mat.
Make a straight line from your head to your knees.
steps: Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows about 45° from your body.
Pause.
Push back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Letting your hips pike up or sag.
exercises.note: Pad your knees on a mat and stop if your wrists hurt.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Hands on your hips or in front of your chest.
steps: Step one foot backward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front shin about vertical.
Push through your front heel to return to standing, then repeat on the same side or alternate.
mistakes: Letting your front knee travel far forward.
exercises.note: Hold a support if you need balance, and use a mat under the back knee.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Spinal Jefferson Curl
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your arms hanging loose.
Tuck your chin gently toward your chest.
steps: Curl your spine down slowly, one segment at a time, letting your arms hang.
Go only as low as feels comfortable for your hamstrings and back.
Roll back up the same way, stacking the spine from the bottom.
cues: Slow, one segment at a time
mistakes: Dropping down fast instead of rolling.
Forcing the range past what feels comfortable.
exercises.note: Stop if you feel pain in your back, and don't do this if you have a recent back injury.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat to Stand
setup: Stand with your feet hip width apart and fold forward to hold your toes.
Keep your chest as high as you can.
steps: Keeping your toes in your hands, bend your knees and sit your hips down into a deep squat.
Lift your chest and straighten your back.
Straighten your legs to rise, keeping hold of your toes.
mistakes: Rounding your back to keep hold of your toes.
exercises.note: Move within your range, and hold a support instead if you can't hold your toes comfortably.

exercises.name: Bounds
setup: Stand tall on a flat, non-slip surface with room to run.
Keep your chest up and arms ready to swing.
steps: Push off one foot and leap forward onto the other with a long stride.
Drive your opposite arm and knee up.
Land softly, then push into the next leap.
mistakes: Taking short steps with no air time.
exercises.note: Warm up first, stay on a forgiving surface, and stop if your calves or knees tighten.

exercises.name: Box Jump
setup: Stand facing a sturdy box about an arm's length away.
Feet hip width apart and arms ready to swing.
steps: Swing your arms back, dip, and jump up onto the box.
Land softly on the whole foot with your knees bent.
Stand tall, then step down one foot at a time.
mistakes: Jumping back down onto the floor.
Landing with your knees caving inward.
Choosing a box height you can't land on cleanly.
exercises.note: Use a sturdy, non-slip box and start low; always step down to protect your Achilles tendons and knees.

exercises.name: Bradford/Rocky Presses (Barbell)
setup: Hold the bar at your shoulders with a grip just outside shoulder width.
Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your core braced.
steps: Dip your knees slightly.
Drive up and press the bar overhead while stepping your feet in.
Lower the bar to your shoulders under control.
mistakes: Dipping forward so the bar travels out front.
Leaning back to press the bar.
Pressing before your legs finish driving.
exercises.note: Use a lighter weight than your strict press, take the bar from a rack, and keep the area clear in case you drop it.

exercises.name: Breaststroke Swim
setup: Float face down with your arms stretched forward.
Keep your hips near the surface.
steps: Pull both arms back together in a keyhole shape.
Bring your knees up and kick your legs out and together.
Glide for a moment, then repeat the cycle.
mistakes: Lifting your head too high so your hips sink.
exercises.note: Swim only where you can do so safely, ideally with a lifeguard on duty or someone nearby.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
setup: Stand tall on a flat surface with your feet hip width apart.
Keep your arms ready to swing.
steps: Swing your arms back and bend your knees.
Swing your arms forward and jump as far as you can.
Land softly with bent knees and hold still for a second.
mistakes: Falling forward or back after landing.
exercises.note: Warm up first, land on a forgiving surface, and stop if your knees or ankles feel sore.

exercises.name: Broomstick Pass-Throughs (Dowel)
setup: Hold a dowel with a very wide grip in front of your thighs.
Stand tall with your ribs down.
steps: Lift the dowel overhead with straight arms.
Move it back behind your body as far as comfortable.
Return it to the front along the same path.
mistakes: Narrowing your grip to force the range.
Arching your lower back to get the arms over.
exercises.note: Widen your grip until the movement is pain-free, and stop if you feel pinching at the front of your shoulder.

exercises.name: Butterfly Swim
setup: Float face down with your arms stretched forward.
Keep your legs together.
steps: Sweep both arms back together in an arc while your legs kick in a dolphin motion.
Breathe forward during the arm recovery.
Repeat in a smooth rhythm.
mistakes: Dropping your elbows during the pull.
Rushing the rhythm so it gets sloppy.
exercises.note: This is a tiring stroke; swim only where you can do so safely, ideally with a lifeguard on duty.

exercises.name: Bar Pushdown (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley high and stand close with a slight lean forward.
Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width, elbows at your sides.
steps: Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze for a moment.
Let the bar rise until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor.
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and the shoulders taking over.
Leaning over the bar and pushing with body weight.
Letting the bar ride up to the face.
exercises.note: Keep your wrists straight and stop if your elbows feel sore at lockout.

exercises.name: Bench Chest Fly (Cable)
setup: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys, a handle in each hand.
Lie back, arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend.
steps: Bring your hands together over your chest in a wide arc.
Squeeze, then open slowly until you feel a stretch.
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows so it becomes a press.
Letting the cable pull the shoulders forward at the stretch.
exercises.note: Don't stretch past the point where the front of the shoulder feels pinched.

exercises.name: Bench Press (Cable)
setup: Set two pulleys at chest height behind the bench.
Lie back with a handle in each hand, elbows around 45–70° from your body.
steps: Press the handles up and slightly together.
Lower with control until your elbows reach just past the line of your torso.
mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward at the top.
Bench set too far back so the cable pulls you.
exercises.note: Pick up the handles carefully and keep tension on the cable as you lie back.

exercises.name: Bench Straight Leg Kickback (Cable)
setup: Attach the ankle strap to a low pulley. Place your hands on the bench, chest leaning over it, working leg straight.
Brace your core.
steps: Kick the working leg straight back and up.
Squeeze your glute at the top.
Lower slowly without letting the stack rest.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to get the leg higher.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light enough that you don't arch your lower back, and check the ankle strap is snug before you move.

exercises.name: Chop (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley high or mid. Stand side-on, both hands on the handle.
Feet wide and braced.
steps: Pull the handle diagonally across your body, turning from your torso.
Finish with arms straight and your chest facing away from the stack.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Letting the weight swing you around.
exercises.note: Rotate through the trunk and hips, not just the lower back.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press (Cable)
setup: Set pulleys at upper-chest height behind a decline bench.
Lie back and hook your feet, handles at chest level.
steps: Press the handles out and slightly down.
Return until your elbows sit just behind your body.
exercises.note: Use a bench with foot pads. A steeper decline isn't needed.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press (Cable)
setup: Set the bench at about 30°, with pulleys low behind it.
Lie back with a handle in each hand at chest level.
steps: Press the handles up and slightly together over your upper chest.
Lower slowly.
cues: Press up along your face line
mistakes: Bench too steep so the shoulders do the work.
exercises.note: Keep the handles under control when you lie back, and use a weight you can press without your shoulders shrugging.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Fly (Cable)
setup: Set both pulleys low and stand in a split stance in the middle with a handle in each hand.
Start with your arms out and down, elbows slightly bent.
steps: Sweep your hands up and together in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower slowly back to the start.
mistakes: Bending your elbows into a curl.
Leaning back to lift the weight.
Letting your hands travel behind your body at the start.
exercises.note: Use a moderate weight and keep your shoulders down; stop if the front of your shoulder feels pinched.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Cable)
setup: Set the pulleys low. Hold the handles at shoulder height, feet in a split stance.
Brace your core.
steps: Press the handles overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower to shoulder height.
exercises.note: Brace your core and use a weight you can press without leaning back, since the cable pulls you forward.

exercises.name: Overhead Straight Bar Extensions (Cable)
setup: Set a low pulley, facing away from it with the bar behind your head.
Elbows pointing forward, upper arms close to your ears.
steps: Extend your arms overhead until straight.
Lower slowly until a deep stretch in the back of the arms.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light, since the loaded position behind your head stresses the elbows and shoulders.

exercises.name: Rope Face Pulls (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley at head height. Grip the rope ends with thumbs toward you.
Step back until tight.
steps: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends apart.
Finish with your hands by your ears.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light so your shoulders stay down, and stop if your shoulders pinch.

exercises.name: Rope Kneeling Face Pull (Cable)
setup: Kneel on a mat facing the high pulley, rope ends in hand.
Sit tall with your back straight.
steps: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends.
Squeeze, then return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light and sit tall on a mat to protect your knees.

exercises.name: Seated Rope Face Pull (Cable)
setup: Sit on a bench or the floor facing a pulley at face height.
Hold the rope with thumbs toward you.
steps: Pull toward your face, splitting the rope.
Hold.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light so your shoulders stay down, and stop if your shoulders pinch.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Cable)
setup: Stand side-on to the stack, holding the handle at your side.
Feet hip width.
steps: Bend sideways away from the stack.
Return to upright by squeezing the side of your trunk.
exercises.note: Keep the load moderate. Stop if you feel pain in the lower back.

exercises.name: Single Arm Neutral Grip Row (Cable)
setup: Sit facing the stack, one handle in a neutral grip.
Sit tall with a slight lean.
steps: Row the handle to your ribs.
Squeeze.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep your torso still and don't twist to move the handle.

exercises.name: Single Arm Rear Delt Row (Cable)
setup: Stand side-on to the stack, handle in the far hand.
Slight hinge.
steps: Pull the handle across your body, elbow high and wide.
Squeeze the rear delt.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep the weight light and the movement controlled; the rear shoulder is small and strains easily.

exercises.name: Single Arm Underhand Grip Row (Cable)
setup: Sit facing the stack, palm up.
Chest tall.
steps: Row to the ribs, elbow tight.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep your torso still and use a weight you can row without twisting.

exercises.name: Standing Low To High Wood Chopper (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley low and stand side-on, holding with both hands.
Feet wide.
steps: Pull diagonally up and across your body.
Rotate from the torso.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Rotate through your hips and trunk, not your lower back, and keep the load moderate.

exercises.name: Standing Single Arm Chest Press (Cable)
setup: Stand side-on to the stack, a handle in your outer hand.
Split stance, brace your core.
steps: Press the handle forward until your arm is straight.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Brace your core so the cable can't twist you, and use a weight you can press without leaning.

exercises.name: Supinating Row (Cable)
setup: Sit at a low pulley, palms facing up.
Chest tall.
steps: Row, turning the palms up as you pull.
Return slowly.
exercises.note: Keep your back flat and don't lean back to finish the row.

exercises.name: Wood Chopper (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley at a high or low setting and stand side-on to the stack.
Hold the handle with both hands and keep your feet wide.
steps: Chop the handle diagonally across your body.
Rotate through your torso and hips.
Return slowly to the start.
mistakes: Letting the weight swing you around.
exercises.note: Keep the load moderate and rotate from your hips, not your lower back.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl (Cable)
setup: Sit on a bench with your forearms resting on your thighs, palms up, holding the bar from a low pulley.
Let your wrists hang over your knees.
steps: Curl your wrists up toward your forearms.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your fingers roll slightly open.
mistakes: Lifting your forearms off your thighs.
exercises.note: Keep the load light to protect your wrists and the tendons in your forearms.

exercises.name: Calf Press (Machine)
setup: Sit and place the balls of your feet on the plate.
Back flat against the pad.
steps: Press up onto your toes.
Lower to a full stretch.
exercises.note: Keep your knees slightly bent instead of locking them, and don't use a weight that makes your heels slip.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
setup: Rest on your forearms on the pads with your back flat against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down.
steps: Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly without swinging.
mistakes: Lifting only the legs without curling the pelvis.
Shrugging your shoulders to your ears.
exercises.note: Keep your back pressed to the pad, and stop if your lower back arches or your shoulders feel pinched.

exercises.name: Cat-Camel
setup: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Keep your neck long.
steps: Arch your back toward the ceiling like a cat, tucking your chin.
Then let your belly drop and lift your chest and tailbone slightly.
Move slowly between the two positions while breathing.
mistakes: Forcing the range at either end.
exercises.note: Move gently, and stop if you feel pain in your back or wrists.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row (Machine)
exercises.equipment: T-bar row machine with chest pad
setup: Lie chest against the pad, feet on the platform.
Hold the handles.
steps: Row the handles to your torso.
Squeeze.
Lower slowly.
exercises.note: Keep your chest on the pad and your neck neutral throughout the set.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Barbell Curl (Barbell)
setup: Grip the bar underhand with your hands about 15 centimetres apart.
Stand tall with elbows at your sides.
steps: Curl the bar toward your shoulders without moving your elbows.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Swinging the bar with your hips.
Bending your wrists at the top.
exercises.note: Keep the weight lighter than a wide-grip curl, since the narrow grip stresses the wrists.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up off a Dumbbell (Dumbbell)
setup: Place your hands close together on a hex dumbbell, in a push-up position.
Make a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Lower your chest toward the dumbbell with elbows close to your sides.
Pause.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.note: Use a hex dumbbell that won't roll, and drop to your knees if your wrists hurt.

exercises.name: Controlled Forearm Pronation and Supination (Dumbbell)
setup: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh, wrist just past the knee.
Hold a light dumbbell upright by one end.
steps: Rotate your forearm so your palm faces up.
Rotate it back until your palm faces down.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
mistakes: Using a weight that is too heavy.
exercises.note: Use a very light dumbbell and stop if you feel pain in the wrist or elbow.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
setup: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width and toes turned out slightly.
Keep your chest up.
steps: Shift your weight to one side and squat deep on that leg.
Keep the other leg straight with the foot flat or toes up.
Push through your heel to return to the middle, then alternate sides.
mistakes: Letting your heel lift off the floor.
Rounding your back as you go down.
exercises.note: Work within your hip range and hold a support if your balance is shaky.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Tricep Extension (Cable)
setup: Set the pulley high and stand side-on to the stack, holding the handle in the far hand across your body.
Pin your upper arm against your side with the elbow bent.
steps: Push the handle down and out to the side until your arm is straight.
Squeeze at lockout.
Let the handle rise slowly back across your body.
mistakes: Leaning your body into the push.
exercises.note: Start light until you can keep your upper arm still through the whole set.

exercises.name: Cuban Press (Dumbbell)
setup: Hold light dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Stand tall with your ribs down.
steps: Lift the dumbbells to chest height with elbows leading, then rotate your hands up so the dumbbells point to the ceiling.
Press overhead.
Reverse the path slowly back to your sides.
mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy.
exercises.note: Use light weights and stop if you feel pinching at the front of your shoulder.

exercises.name: Cycling Cooldown (Cardio)
setup: Set the seat height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit tall with relaxed shoulders and loose hands on the bars.
steps: Pedal at a moderate pace for a minute.
Lower the resistance gradually and slow your cadence over about five minutes.
Finish with a slow spin before stepping off.
exercises.note: Don't stop abruptly after hard work; keep moving gently until your breathing settles.

exercises.name: Cycling Intervals (Cardio)
setup: Set the seat height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up for five minutes before the first hard effort.
steps: Pedal hard for the work period, such as 30 seconds.
Slow to an easy spin for the recovery period.
Repeat for the number of rounds you planned.
mistakes: Starting the first interval too hard to repeat.
exercises.note: Stop if you feel dizzy or chest pain, and cool down with a few easy minutes afterwards.

exercises.name: Cycling Sprint (Cardio)
setup: Set the seat height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up properly for five to ten minutes before sprinting.
steps: Build speed over a few seconds, then go all out for the sprint.
Ease off and spin easily to recover.
Repeat with a full recovery between sprints.
mistakes: Standing on the pedals with a loose seat.
exercises.note: Warm up first, and stop if you feel faint, dizzy or any chest pain.

exercises.name: Cycling Warmup (Cardio)
setup: Set the seat height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Keep the resistance very light at the start.
steps: Pedal at an easy pace.
Increase the cadence and resistance slowly over five to ten minutes.
Finish when your breathing is slightly elevated.
mistakes: Pedalling with the knees pinching in.

exercises.name: Dead Bug (Weighted) (Dumbbell)
setup: Lie on your back with a light dumbbell held above your chest in both hands and your knees bent above your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the mat.
steps: Extend one leg toward the floor while lowering the opposite arm overhead.
Return to the start.
Alternate sides slowly.
mistakes: Letting your lower back arch off the floor.
Using a dumbbell that is too heavy.
exercises.note: Hold the dumbbell with both hands, keep it light, and stop if your lower back arches.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift (Barbell)
setup: Stand on a low platform with the bar over your midfoot.
Grip just outside your legs.
steps: Brace and push the floor away.
Stand tall.
Lower under control.
exercises.note: Use a lighter weight than your normal deadlift.

exercises.name: Alternating Forward Lunge (Dumbbell)
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
steps: Step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front heel to step back to the start.
Alternate legs.
